If Agno consumes the returned stream by calling internal workflow execution helpers (e.g., `_aexecute_stream`) during iteration, `_FOREGROUND_WORKFLOW_ACTIVE` will be `False` and the new background wrappers can create duplicate workflow spans. Keep the ContextVar active for the entire lifetime of the stream (until the wrapper stops/fails), e.g., by keeping the token and resetting it from the wrapper when iteration completes (or by extending the wrapper to accept an on-finish callback that restores the previous value).

Ok so you can pass an agent to a workflow.. and then the agent decides whether to actually invoke the workflow or not.. and we already have that second nested invocation captured as a `execute_tool invoke_workflow` so we should be suppressing the nested call like you said..

I've fixed this by storing the workflow run ids in the context instead of the instance(id) on the workflow object.. Run ID is better than instance(id) because instance(id) is just the id of the workflow object and the same object can have multiple concurrent runs (and in some scenarios the context can leak).. So this fixes that bug which is nice...

In order to clean up / remove these run IDs from the context when the workflow finishes, I had to add `self_on_close` back to the streaming run so we have a hook for when the streaming workflow finishes..

Also before agno `2.3.9` (released December 2025) there was no run id, so I bumped the supported agno version to `2.3.9`.. LMK what you think.. we can go back to using instance id to support lower versions but it is a little buggy..

Agno has a lot of complexity on these workflows.. async, sync, streaming, pausing/resuming, background execution, agents being passed to workflows.. neasted executions.. kind of a pain to deal with it all
